content.value_statement: Teams often miss critical coverage while adding features quickly. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create focused Pest tests for important behavior.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of Pest tests in Feature and Unit test directories.
Focuses tests on user workflows, business paths, validation rules, and API endpoints.
Encourages descriptive test names that explain expected behavior.
Supports mocking databases, APIs, file systems, and services when needed.
Uses datasets to cover multiple scenarios with less duplicated test structure.
Prioritizes behavior and outcomes over implementation details.
limitations: It provides testing guidance, not a complete automated test generator.
It assumes Pest and a compatible PHP project are already available.
It does not define project-specific factories, fixtures, or application state.
It references external testing guidance through a parent-directory link.

use_cases.title: Cover A New Feature
use_cases.description: Create focused Pest tests for the core workflow before marking a feature complete.

use_cases.title: Protect Business Rules
use_cases.description: Write unit tests for validation, branching logic, and outcome-based behavior.

use_cases.title: Review Test Strategy
use_cases.description: Decide which critical paths deserve coverage and which edge cases can wait.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Feature Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs coverage for one user flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write Pest feature tests for this workflow. Focus on the happy path, one failure case, and clear behavior names.

prompt_templates.title: Add Unit Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs fast tests for business logic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write Pest unit tests for this business rule. Mock external services and test observable outcomes only.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Completion Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: A feature is nearly ready to ship.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature and propose the minimum Pest tests needed before completion. Prioritize critical paths and validation behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Existing Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user wants stronger tests without brittle assertions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Pest tests for gaps, fragile implementation details, missing mocks, and opportunities to use datasets.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for tests for user registration.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest feature tests for successful registration, validation failures, and any required external service mock.

output_examples.input: A team asks which tests are needed before release.
output_examples.output: The skill would identify core workflows, business rules, and API behavior that need coverage before feature completion.

output_examples.input: A developer shares brittle tests tied to private methods.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend outcome-based assertions and simpler tests that avoid implementation details.

best_practices: Start with critical user paths before covering small utilities.
Name tests with clear behavior and expected outcomes.
Mock external dependencies so tests stay fast and reliable.
anti_patterns: Writing broad tests that assert private implementation details.
Skipping validation and failure cases for critical workflows.
Adding many slow integration tests when focused unit tests are enough.

faq.question: Which framework does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Pest tests for PHP projects, including feature and unit test workflows.

faq.question: Can it choose what needs test coverage?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps prioritize critical user workflows, business logic, validation rules, and API endpoints.

faq.question: Does it write exhaustive tests for every edge case?
faq.answer: No. It favors focused coverage and defers non-critical utilities unless coverage is required.

faq.question: Can it help with mocks?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides mocking for databases, APIs, file systems, services, and other external dependencies.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What should authors fix before publishing?
faq.answer: Authors should replace the parent-directory documentation link with packaged or reviewed guidance.
